entwurf.thema: The founding of the Lego Group and Ole Kirk Christiansen's shift from wooden toys to plastic bricks

teile.text: Before Lego’s famous plastic bricks, Ole Kirk Christiansen crafted wooden toys in Billund.
teile.name: Ole Kirk Christiansen
teile.szene: The presenter, a blue-eyed man in a grey suit and fedora, stands in a dusty 1930s Danish workshop. He holds a carved wooden toy duck while sunlight filters through a grimy window.

teile.text: In 1934 he renamed the workshop Lego, meaning ‘play well’ in Danish.
teile.name: Wooden Workshop
teile.szene: Close-up of a carpenter’s weathered hands carefully carving a wooden toy horse. Shavings fall onto a workbench littered with hand tools and wooden blocks in a dim workshop.

teile.text: Two years later, he added production after buying an injection‑molding machine.
teile.name: Lego Naming
teile.szene: A quiet 1930s Billund street scene. A simple wooden sign above a workshop door reads LEGO in clean lettering. A child walks past holding a small wooden pull-toy.

teile.text: What changed the humble toys into a system for endless building?
teile.name: Plastic Skepticism
teile.szene: A man in a 1950s suit sits at a desk with a typewriter, shaking his head at a plastic brick. Shelves of traditional wooden toys are behind him.

teile.text: In 1949 Lego released interlocking bricks inspired by Hilary Page’s 1939 design, and in 1958 patented the ABS brick.
teile.name: Early Plastic
teile.szene: A large, metallic injection-molding machine operates in a factory. Small, translucent plastic bricks spill into a wooden crate as a worker in 1940s attire watches the process.

teile.text: These sturdy bricks let builders craft vehicles, buildings and robots, driving Lego to become the largest toy maker.
teile.name: Modern Lego
teile.szene: A bright, modern room where colorful interlocking plastic bricks are scattered on a table. A father and son are building a complex structure together in soft daylight.

teile.name: Call to Action
teile.szene: The presenter in his fedora and grey suit smiles, holding a finished model of a colorful house. He adjusts his gold pocket watch as the camera zooms in.

entwurf.beschreibung: Ole Kirk Christiansen began with wooden toys, added plastic production in 1947, and his son later refined the modern brick design, helping Lego become the world’s largest toy manufacturer.
